correctness.rationale: Exact moments gamma_0=1, gamma_1=c/2+d, gamma_j=c/(j+1) for j>=2. The r=1 Jacobi Gram-rank-one test gives H1; the r=0 Legendre inverse-Gram Schur complement gives H2. Higher starts are positive moments of c*t^r dt. Two exact scalar Agler differences give C. For 0<c<=1 the lower H2 root lies below H1, giving exact intervals and explicitly expanded k^-4/k^-3 versus n^-2/n^-1 windows, with c=1 degeneracy. All-order subnormality follows from the explicit measure c dt+(1-c)delta_0. The included verifier passed 315 exact and finite assertions; tests alone are not the proof.

value.rationale: Independent variation of the first two Bergman-tail weights creates two simultaneous finite-order moment obstructions, unlike the classic one-weight family. The exact all-orders quantitative windows show side-dependent convergence to the subnormal locus and a critical change of the exponent at continuous mass c=1. This answers a natural stability and hierarchy comparison question; it is not just a single numerical k case or a restated general rank-one perturbation.
